findingsAndVerificationQuestions.detail: New deliver-handoff and reobserve-handoff CLI actions require a project ID and reject caller-supplied event IDs, messages, URLs, source task IDs and force options.

Handoff delivery validates the retained journal request against the registered owner, paired target, exact event, generation, message and event type. A pre-submit callback rechecks selection and policy.

Scoped runtime selection distinguishes handoffs from continuations and review events. Added tests cover changed selection, sibling queue isolation, invalid event roles and replay refusal after known or uncertain outcomes.

The new reobservation path takes a registry registration lock and invokes a commit callback. The exact callback's transitive locking behavior was not inspected. Absence of lock inversion or deadlock is not independently established.

The before-submit callback uses separate journal, registration, target and policy observations. Its behavior under concurrent modification requires cross-module verification. No exploitable race is established by this diff alone.
The added tests exercise selected runtime paths with a fake adapter. Installed browser behavior, process crashes, durable recovery and cross-process concurrency were not independently tested.

findingsAndVerificationQuestions.detail: Supervisor workspace identity now resolves existing directory components and hashes their observed spelling. This addresses case-only aliases while preserving distinct case-sensitive sibling directories.

The supervisor acquires canonical and legacy named mutexes, retaining both until release. Failed second acquisition releases the first mutex. This provides transitional compatibility with matching legacy monitor identities.
The lifecycle facade retains historical task names, Run-key names and launch arguments. It additionally checks the supervisor's canonical mutex identity when reporting whether a monitor is running.

A legacy monitor started through another case spelling can hold a different legacy mutex while the new monitor acquires the canonical mutex. Full interoperability with all already-running legacy case aliases is therefore not established.

Canonical identity relies on Directory.GetDirectories with a component search pattern rather than a retained directory handle. Directory replacement races and wildcard-containing components require independent examination.

The facade extracts a function from the supervisor's parsed PowerShell AST and executes it as a scriptblock. The source checks its file type and reparse attribute, but does not demonstrate pinned file identity against concurrent replacement.
Real cross-process tests cover case aliases, independent workspaces, release and matching legacy reservations. They do not establish every migration, crash or concurrent replacement scenario.
